name: Lamech
overview: Lamech was a male descendant of Methushael, identified as his son according to Genesis 4:18. Scripture presents him as a figure within the early genealogies of humanity, with no specific tribal affiliation or additional notes provided.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Lamech' appears simply as a proper name in Scripture, with no explicit meaning or divine origin noted in the biblical text referenced (Genesis 4:18). Therefore, it is presented plainly without further theological significance attached to its meaning.
familyAndRelationships: Lamech was the son of Methushael and husband to two women, Adah and Zillah. He fathered four children: Jabal, Jubal, Tubal-cain, and Naamah, as recorded in Genesis 4:18-22. These relationships situate him as a patriarchal figure in the early biblical narrative.
scriptureSignificance: Lamech holds significance as part of the early human lineage, notably as the father of Noah, through whom God would bring comfort and restoration following the curse on the ground. His prophetic naming of Noah reflects a faith in God's plan to relieve humanity's fallen condition, highlighting Lamech's role in the unfolding redemptive history. His lifespan and death shortly before the flood mark him as a transitional figure between the antediluvian world and God's judgment and renewal.
